finding.title: Close the update-mutation and create-validation gaps on append-only event collections in firestore.rules

evidence.quote: // deny `update` and `delete`. Snapshot collections deny `delete` and gate

finding.why: completions, streak_events, learning_ledger and points_ledger all `allow update` for the owner with no check that the update reproduces the existing document (no comparison against `resource.data`), so any client holding the owner's valid session -- a modified build, a tampered/replayed request, or a future client bug -- can overwrite an already-committed event with different field values. Three of the four (streak_events, learning_ledger, points_ledger) validate literally nothing on create either: no presence check, no `is timestamp`, no `<= request.time` bound, contradicting SR-3. Because points_ledger backs the reward-redemption economy, the append-only invariant this collection family exists to guarantee is not enforced -- a user could rewrite their own point-earning history to inflate reward-eligible balances. The file's own top-of-file comment ('deny `update` and `delete`') is simply false for the current rule bodies, which is itself a sign this drifted from the original design during the permission-denied-outage fixes documented inline at streak_events.
finding.recommendation: Restrict `update` on all four collections to a byte-identical replay of the existing doc (or drop `update` once outbox retries are proven to only ever hit `create`), and add `is timestamp` + presence + `<= request.time` validation on create for streak_events/learning_ledger/points_ledger, matching what completions partially does today. Fix the stale line-38 comment.
acceptance_criteria: functions/test/firestore_rules.test.mjs asserts that updating an existing completions/streak_events/learning_ledger/points_ledger doc with a changed field value is denied.
A create with a missing/non-timestamp/future created_at on streak_events, learning_ledger, or points_ledger is denied.
